ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual PEP screening under Articles L. 561-10, L. 561-11 and R. 561-14 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Sanctions screening must cover the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) 833/2014), French domestic asset-freeze orders published by the Direction générale du Trésor, UN Security Council consolidated lists, and, for any USD-denominated transaction or US nexus, the OFAC SDN list. Enhanced due diligence requiring senior management approval and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth analysis is mandatory where a PEP, higher-risk third country, or unusual transaction pattern is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the INPI data portal (data.inpi.fr); pre-clearance search consultation via Infogreffe/RCS extracts and the RNCS database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin script and be capable of being recorded in French registry systems. Non-Latin scripts are not accepted for the legal name; foreign names must be accompanied by a French transliteration or, where a French name is impossible, a French-language translation of the activity is required in the RCS filing. The words Société par Actions Simplifiée or the abbreviation SAS must appear in the instruments and in all public registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Guichet Unique or the Registrar, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within one month of the rejection notice. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may bring a summary action (référé) before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce or, where no commercial court exists, the Tribunal Judiciaire, relying on Articles L. 123-3 and R. 123-6 of the French Commercial Code. In parallel, the applicant may re-submit with a new name to preserve the incorporation timeline; a fresh 30-day reservation window applies to any newly cleared alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a formal domiciliation agreement with a licensed corporate domiciliation provider (office de domiciliation) for a renewable period of up to five years. This is assessed as acceptable for an ISIC 4661 wholesale bitumen trading entity, provided the registered office maintains a physical French address for official correspondence, legal notices, tax administration, and inspection access. A pure virtual office without substantive local management and records increases French tax residence and permanent establishment exposure for the non-resident shareholders.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate; approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection where a physical registered office and accounting records are maintained. The likelihood rises above 30% if the SAS is domiciliated virtually with no substantive French activity, because anti-fraud services (Tracfin and social/tax units) may verify commercial substance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; online service portals include impots.gouv.fr for corporate tax and VAT administration and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr for company formation and SIREN/SIRET registration via the INPI Guichet Unique.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS owned by foreign entities, incorporation is effected by filing the proposed articles of association with the INPI Guichet Unique through an appointed legal representative and registered office; the registry issues a Kbis extract containing the SIREN/SIRET identification number. The DGFiP then automatically allocates the French intra-community VAT number (Numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) to the established taxable person. A non-established branch or a direct foreign taxable person must apply separately using form P0i/SiREU to the competent non-resident business tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) to obtain a direct VAT ID, along with appointment of a tax representative where required, followed by registration for business rates (CFE) and, if applicable, corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French SAS status is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax, and no US-style check-the-box election exists. Available elections include fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223 A for holding companies owning at least 95% of French subsidiaries, the option to form a single VAT-group (assujetti unique) with affiliated taxable persons, and elections under applicable double-tax-treaty rules for allocating profits or claiming foreign tax credits. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by the EU ATAD regime and French Art. 212 bis CGI denial rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) as enacted under the Code Général des Impôts (CGI Art. 256-283) and harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (no minimum threshold for an established French taxable person; registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction). For non-established EU suppliers undertaking distance sales to private consumers, the EU OSS cross-border threshold is EUR 10,000; non-EU suppliers have no threshold and must register for any taxable supply in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting for French-established taxable persons under the national reform governed by CGI Art. 289 and implementing circulars. B2B invoices must be issued through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the national public portal (FNFE), using structured data formats such as Factur-X, EDI/UBL, or equivalent, with transaction-level data transmitted to DGFiP for pre-validation and VAT monitoring. No physical fiscal stamping or real-time revenue clearance machine is currently imposed for standard containerised wholesale exports; however, the digital transmission to DGFiP and the PDP of invoice data constitutes mandatory functional fiscal clearance, with interoperability based on the FNFE API specifications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under CGI Art. 262-I-1, a supply of goods qualifies for the 0% French export VAT rate only if the goods are physically dispatched or transported from French/EU territory to a non-EU destination, the exporter holds a valid customs export declaration accepted by French Customs (DGDDI), and the exporter retains conclusive evidence that the goods left the EU within the prescribed period. For containerised bitumen and asphalt in drums or bags, the SAS must demonstrate legal title sale to the foreign buyer, container-level transport from the French port of loading to the third-country destination, and coherence between the invoiced quantities, the customs declaration, and the outbound logistics documents. Directly connected offshore services (including freight and handling services for the exported goods) can also be zero-rated under CGII Art. 262-II where the recipient of those services is a non-EU customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/ENS) accepted and released by French Customs, containing the container numbers and the final non-EU destination
Bill of Lading (or equivalent multimodal CMR/through transport document) evidencing carriage of the containerised bitumen out of the EU to the foreign buyer's port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 bank notification proving collection of the export sale proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French Customs (DGDDI) and DGFiP cross-reference export declarations, Bill of Lading data, and VAT refund/zero-ration claims through electronic matching systems; audit triggers include missing transport evidence, shipment to high-risk destinations, margin anomalies, and incomplete FX receipts. An unjustified export zero-rating is retrospectively reversed by issuing a VAT assessment: French VAT at 20% becomes immediately due together with late interest at 0.2% per month, a general insufficiency penalty of 40%, and an 80% increase for bad-faith misconduct or organized fraud. The standard three-year tax recovery period is extended to six years where fraudulent intent is shown, and criminal fiscal prosecution under CGI Art. 1741 can be brought concurrently.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, as the French central bank within the Eurosystem, under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and international financial regulatory functions are also allocated to the French Treasury Directorate-General and the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions within the framework of EU law. Current-account payments, including imports, exports, freight, insurance, services, dividends, interest, and royalties, are generally freely transferable. Capital movements involving EU and third-country jurisdictions are generally permitted, subject to anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax, customs, beneficial-ownership, financial-accounting, and statistical-reporting requirements. A French SAS may generally receive foreign investment, maintain foreign-currency accounts, pay non-resident suppliers, repay shareholder loans, and remit dividends after approval of annual accounts, satisfaction of creditor-protection requirements, withholding-tax analysis, and confirmation that distributable profits exist. Banks may require contracts, invoices, customs evidence, board resolutions, shareholder registers, tax residency certificates, transfer-pricing support, and source-of-funds evidence before executing or releasing transfers. Payments involving sanctioned parties, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque ownership, unusual trade routes, over-invoicing, under-invoicing, or unexplained third-party settlement may be rejected or reported. Dividend, interest, royalty, and service-fee remittances remain subject to French tax, treaty, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and transfer-pricing rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no general deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's commercial discretion. The company must maintain complete commercial, customs, accounting, VAT, sanctions-screening, and bank-payment records and comply with applicable statistical, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering reporting obligations. Specific obligations may arise for cash or bearer instruments, regulated goods, sanctions-related transactions, external statistical reporting, customs declarations, or transactions involving restricted jurisdictions. Cross-border cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more entering or leaving the EU require the applicable customs declaration, and French customs or financial-intelligence reporting requirements may apply to suspicious or inadequately documented transactions. Bank-specific cut-off, documentary, and transaction-monitoring controls do not constitute a statutory currency-surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
BPCE S.A., including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne networks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and foreign-currency collection; low as the sole treasury bank for a newly incorporated, foreign-owned French SAS engaged in physical commodity trading. An EU-licensed electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, card services, foreign-exchange conversion, and certain cross-border payment services, but it is not necessarily a deposit-taking bank and client-funds safeguarding is not equivalent to deposit insurance. An offshore digital EMI without EU passporting, an EU establishment, or a licensed payment partner cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to the French company on a cross-border basis merely through an application interface. EMIs may restrict commodity trading, high-value international wires, cash-intensive activity, sanctioned corridors, third-party payments, and transactions lacking customs or invoice evidence. Maintain a regulated French or EU bank as the primary account for capital, payroll, taxes, letters of credit, and emergency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically appear at a bank branch to open an account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can reliably verify identity, authority, beneficial ownership, registered office, business purpose, source of funds, and expected transaction profile using acceptable electronic identification and documentary controls. In practice, banks may require a video interview, certified identity documents, qualified electronic signatures, a French contact person, an in-person meeting, or a visit by the legal representative, particularly for a newly incorporated SAS, non-resident shareholders, complex ownership, commodity trading, high expected turnover, or third-country payment flows. Capital escrow arrangements may require original or certified corporate documents and a French notary, lawyer, or formation agent. The bank retains discretion to decline or delay onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent beneficial-ownership information, including a corporate shareholder chain that does not clearly identify natural persons exercising ultimate control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; statutes; cap table; shareholder register; group ownership chart to natural persons; ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations; passports and address evidence for relevant individuals; board or shareholder resolutions; and evidence of registration in the French beneficial-ownership register where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors, shareholders, or authorized signatories with no clear French nexus or an unexplained registered-office arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate documents; director appointment evidence; residence and address verification; French lease or domiciliation agreement; explanation of management location; powers of attorney; tax identification details; business-plan rationale for France; and contact details for the French legal, accounting, and logistics functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Physical commodity trading in bitumen or asphalt with high transaction values, unusual routes, intermediary chains, or counterparties in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product description and HS classifications; supplier and customer lists; executed sale and purchase contracts; purchase orders; invoices; bills of lading; certificates of origin; customs declarations; transport and insurance documents; sanctions-screening records; Incoterms; pricing methodology; margin analysis; and documented end-use and destination controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected turnover, payment volumes, currencies, or jurisdictions materially exceeding the initial business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; twelve-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume matrix; currency and corridor analysis; customer and supplier concentration report; financing evidence; audited or management accounts; tax registrations; and periodic variance explanations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital from third parties, shareholder loans with unclear terms, or payments routed through unrelated entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or loan agreement; shareholder and lender identity evidence; bank statements demonstrating source of funds; corporate approvals; capital contribution or loan-purpose documentation; repayment schedule; arm's-length interest support; and written explanation for any third-party payment with matching contractual authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, dual-use, politically exposed person, adverse-media, or high-risk-jurisdiction exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; ownership and control screening; sanctions and PEP screening logs; end-user statements; export-control classification; route and vessel screening; compliance policy; escalation records; and legal analysis demonstrating that the transaction is permitted under EU and French measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax transparency or regulatory inconsistencies, including missing VAT, EORI, tax-residence, or financial-accounting information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax identification and VAT registration where applicable; EORI number; tax-residence certificates; accounting engagement letter; VAT and customs process map; transfer-pricing policy; annual accounts or opening balance sheet; and evidence of compliance with DAC, CRS, FATCA, and applicable reporting obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash settlement, excessive cash withdrawals, rapid pass-through activity, or unexplained payment reversals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal and cash settlement; payment-approval matrix; segregation-of-duties policy; bank reconciliation procedure; customer and supplier payment instructions; refund protocol; transaction-monitoring rules; and documented commercial explanations for any exceptional reversal.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For share capital, use the French SAS capital-deposit account opened in the company's formation name or through the appointed formation professional. Transfer funds from the shareholder's own account by SEPA or SWIFT, identify the payment as share capital subscription, and provide the subscription agreement, shareholder resolution, draft statutes, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and bank transfer confirmation. Obtain the deposit certificate before registration or capital release, then migrate funds to the operational account after incorporation and bank verification. For capital increases, use the approved issuance documentation, subscription records, corporate resolutions, and updated capital records. For shareholder loans, use a separately documented loan agreement, transfer from the lender's account, commercial purpose, maturity, interest, repayment terms, withholding-tax analysis, and related-party transfer-pricing support. Use ISO 20022 payment information or SWIFT free-text remittance information; France has no universal foreign-exchange purpose-code regime for ordinary corporate capital injections. The bank may assign internal transaction categories and request confirmation of the economic purpose. Screen all originators, beneficiaries, banks, intermediaries, and jurisdictions before release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border payment rails for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. A SWIFT MT103 is the legacy customer-credit-transfer format; ISO 20022 pacs.008 is increasingly used as the corresponding structured payment format. Include complete originator and beneficiary information, invoice number, contract reference, Incoterms, shipment or bill-of-lading reference, currency, and payment purpose. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit through SWIFT MT700 or the bank's ISO 20022 trade-finance equivalent, with amendment, document presentation, discrepancy, and confirmation procedures agreed in advance. Match payment parties to the underlying invoice and shipping documents; avoid unrelated third-party settlement unless contractually justified and pre-cleared. Banks may require purchase contracts, invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, certificates of origin, insurance documents, sanctions checks, and proof of delivery. Reconcile all payments to the ERP, retain records under applicable French accounting, AML, tax, customs, and trade-finance retention rules, and apply maker-checker approval for high-value wires.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an EU-regulated bank or eligible investment firm, documented against forecast or contracted exposures and subject to counterparty limits, suitability or appropriateness controls where applicable, ISDA or bank master terms, valuation, collateral, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are not freely deliverable or where settlement is contractually made in a reference currency, provided the transaction is entered into with an authorized counterparty and complies with applicable MiFID II, EMIR, sanctions, market-conduct, and reporting requirements.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for recurring or longer-term funding exposures, subject to board approval, documented hedging purpose, counterparty credit limits, collateral or margin terms, valuation controls, and EMIR clearing, reporting, risk-mitigation, and documentation requirements where applicable.
FX spot transactions and rolling short-dated forwards for invoice settlement and working-capital management, supported by an approved treasury policy and exposure documentation.

Currency options, collars, and option combinations where permitted by the regulated counterparty, subject to product governance, cost and risk disclosure, authorization limits, valuation controls, and documented prohibition of speculative activity unless expressly approved.

Hedging restrictions: do not use derivatives to disguise capital transfers, circumvent sanctions, create unapproved leverage, or speculate beyond documented commercial exposures. Maintain confirmations, valuations, hedge-designation records, collateral records, counterparty due diligence, and periodic effectiveness testing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a EUR 1,500 fine, increased to EUR 3,000 for a repeated breach, court injunctions subject to daily penalties, and possible removal from the Commercial Register after applicable formal procedures. No automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; electronic filing is mandatory, subject to the applicable tax calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge and late-payment interest, currently calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and aggravating circumstances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net annual turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional audit requirements may apply to parent companies, significant subsidiaries, or entities within qualifying corporate groups.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Accounting Standards issued by the Autorité des normes comptables (ANC) apply to separate statutory accounts. IFRS may generally be used for consolidated accounts by eligible non-listed groups and is mandatory for qualifying listed consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a routine annual UBO confirmation. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file initial or amended information through the Guichet unique within the applicable statutory period, generally within 30 days after a change. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities movement register and individual shareholder accounts, with corresponding corporate approvals and filings where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of securities movements and individual shareholder accounts
Register or bound minutes of shareholder decisions and corporate body decisions
Register of beneficial owners and supporting identification records
Corporate accounting books and supporting accounting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500-12,000 per year, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small company may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable ownership, turnover and capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary French SAS conducting wholesale bitumen trading. Qualifying small companies may benefit from the 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. Research and development activities may qualify for the research tax credit. Certain investment, energy-transition and regional schemes may provide separate credits or deductions subject to statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, together with the 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD tax computation schedules and 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD balance-sheet schedules, filed electronically through the French business tax portal using EDI-TDFC or the applicable tax-account interface.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due on the second business day after 1 May. For other year-ends, the return is generally due within three months after the year-end. The electronic filing calendar published by the French tax administration controls the precise date. The final corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, French tax identification number, SIREN number, legal form as Société par Actions Simplifiée, financial year dates and principal activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS files as a French resident taxpayer. The foreign shareholder's address and tax residence are not substituted for the SAS registered office. Report the French SIREN and tax identification numbers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for tax purposes, taxable income, tax losses utilized and corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French-company income and deductible expenses determined under French tax rules. Transactions with foreign related parties must be reconciled to the statutory accounts and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting result to taxable result, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, financial expense limitations and prior-year loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder-level income and unrelated foreign-company accounts. Apply French limits for interest deductions, non-deductible penalties, luxury expenses and provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward or carried back and the portion used in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French losses are generally carried forward without a general time limit but subject to an annual utilization cap, ordinarily EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding year and subject to statutory limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions and other amounts deductible from corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by statutory eligibility and contemporaneous records. Foreign tax credits normally depend on the applicable tax treaty and cannot be claimed merely because foreign tax was commercially incurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, shareholdings, capital gains, retained earnings and balance-sheet tax information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French SAS assets and liabilities on a statutory-accounting basis. Related-party receivables, payables and financing must be consistent with intercompany agreements and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD, corporate income tax payment statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and payment of the final corporate income tax balance and any applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French company's tax account and approved electronic payment method. A foreign parent cannot substitute its own tax account for the French SAS account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of controlled transactions, related-party jurisdictions, transaction categories, amounts and transfer-pricing method where the statutory filing threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border purchases, sales, royalties, services, guarantees, loans and other controlled transactions. Amounts must reconcile to the general ledger, statutory accounts and Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of certain withholding taxes, including payments to non-residents where French withholding applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief only after verifying beneficial ownership, treaty residence and applicable procedural requirements. Retain residence certificates, declarations and payment-level evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge on tax due, which may increase to 40% after formal notice and 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct or abusive non-compliance. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Incorrect returns may also trigger tax reassessment, interest, specific information-return penalties and criminal exposure for fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. A qualifying EU corporate parent may generally obtain exemption where the statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, verify the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, minimum participation and anti-abuse status. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and complete the French administrative forms or treaty-relief procedure required for the payment. Where relief at source is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate, remit the tax to the French tax authority, and support any refund or reclaim with the residence certificate, dividend documentation, ownership evidence and proof of beneficial ownership. Maintain records for the statutory audit and limitation periods.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on qualifying royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty modification and special rules for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Ordinary cross-border interest paid by a French company is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to certain non-cooperative jurisdictions, profit-participating instruments, disguised distributions and anti-abuse situations. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income classification; the applicable treaty must be reviewed before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full French transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity's annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets is at least EUR 150 million, or where it belongs to, controls or is controlled by an enterprise meeting the statutory EUR 150 million threshold, subject to the detailed conditions of the French Tax Code. The annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at the EUR 50 million threshold or where the entity is connected with an enterprise meeting the relevant statutory threshold. Controlled transactions may remain subject to the arm's-length principle and documentation requirements below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to a separate ESR statute. Substance is enforced through the arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership requirements, the general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules, anti-hybrid rules and treaty principal-purpose tests. The SAS should maintain genuine French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or documented operational infrastructure, commercial risk management, bank-account control, books and records, and evidence that its bitumen procurement, logistics, inventory and customer functions are actually performed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating purchase invoices, understating inventory, diverting customer payments, maintaining parallel books or knowingly filing materially false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% for deliberate misconduct to 80% for fraudulent conduct or certain abusive arrangements, and potential criminal tax-fraud prosecution. Serious tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to seven years and a criminal fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions and judicial determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, personal tax-payment liability for fraudulent or repeated non-compliance under French tax law, management-ban orders and, in appropriate cases, travel restrictions imposed by judicial authorities. Limited liability does not protect intentional fraud or personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value Added Tax Fraud and Missing-Trader Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming fictitious input VAT, issuing invoices without genuine supplies, misclassifying cross-border goods, manipulating intra-EU acquisitions or failing to account for import VAT and customs documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid VAT, denial of input-tax credit, interest, 40% or 80% penalties depending on conduct, possible joint-liability measures and criminal prosecution for organized or fraudulent VAT schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who knowingly participate may face criminal fines, imprisonment, civil recovery and management disqualification. Directors may be pursued personally where their conduct caused or facilitated the tax loss.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting French profit through excessive management fees, royalties, financing charges, low-margin related-party resale prices, undocumented guarantees or non-arm's-length commodity pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length taxable profit, withholding-tax exposure, interest, documentation-related penalties and, where applicable, a penalty of up to 5% of the profits transferred or the statutory minimum amount, subject to the governing provisions and procedural findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they deliberately approve sham arrangements, falsify records or organize tax fraud. A mere unsuccessful pricing position, without fraud or gross misconduct, does not ordinarily create automatic personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Beneficial Ownership and Abuse of Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS with no genuine activity, routing dividends or royalties through conduit entities, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner or claiming treaty benefits contrary to the principal purpose of the arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, recharacterization of income, withholding-tax assessment, anti-abuse penalties, interest, potential abuse-of-law surcharge and criminal sanctions where concealment or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil claims, criminal prosecution, management bans, asset-seizure measures and judicial travel restrictions where they knowingly operate a sham structure or conceal beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, bypassing customer due diligence, concealing beneficial owners, processing sanctions-sensitive payments or failing to report serious suspicions to TRACFIN when legally required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory and administrative sanctions, transaction blocking, confiscation, criminal prosecution for money laundering or terrorist financing, fines and imprisonment. Applicable penalties depend on the underlying offense and the person's participation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be individually prosecuted for knowing facilitation, concealment or negligent failure where a specific statutory duty applies. Corporate status does not shield intentional AML offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring bitumen origin, customs value, tariff classification or quantity; falsifying documents; routing goods through sanctioned counterparties; or ignoring EU sanctions and export-control restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, seizure, forfeiture, administrative fines, loss of customs simplifications and criminal sanctions. Sanctions violations may carry substantial fines and imprisonment depending on the measure breached and the conduct involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may be personally prosecuted, fined, disqualified or subject to asset restraint where they authorize or knowingly tolerate customs or sanctions violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain statutory accounts, omission of annual accounts filing, unlawful distributions, insolvency concealment, asset diversion or continuation of trading while insolvent without appropriate action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil damages, accounting penalties, nullity or recovery of unlawful distributions, insolvency clawback, management-liability proceedings, bans on managing companies and criminal sanctions for specified offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to all or part of an insolvency shortfall for management faults, prohibited from managing companies, ordered to repay diverted assets and, for serious misconduct, imprisoned or fined.
